architecture.mechanism: Continuous-curvature (clothoid) target-tree path planning eliminates curvature discontinuity so the vehicle parks accurately and terminates motion smoothly at the goal.
architecture.intervention: Replace the circular/straight-segment parking paths in the automated stop-and-park maneuver with clothoid-based continuous-curvature target-tree paths, so the vehicle arrives at the parking goal accurately and at a complete, discontinuity-free stop before the parking mechanism is engaged.
architecture.expected_effect: Because the vehicle reaches the goal at zero speed without curvature-induced residual motion or oscillation, the transmission park pawl engages cleanly and holds the vehicle, preventing unintended rollaway on a flat surface with the selector in park.
architecture.falsification_test: On a flat surface, run repeated automated park maneuvers with the clothoid target-tree planner, logging vehicle speed at park engagement and post-engagement rollaway distance; if any run shows nonzero speed at engagement, measurable rollaway, or no improvement versus a circular/straight-path baseline, the mechanism is falsified.

challenge.kill_reason: the mechanism-space distinctness adjudication counts 0 materially distinct mechanism(s) (< 2, mechanism_distinctness/2.0.0) — the run generated nothing worth attacking (Art. LXXXIV, R514)
